transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I’m here because I’ve been having some thoughts that are scaring me. Like… sometimes I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And on the drive home, I catch myself wondering if my family or my students might be better off without me.

I don’t want to act on it. But it frightened me enough to come in.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up or wondering if others would be better off without you?
About… a year and a half. Maybe a bit more. It started after I took on the STEM assessment redesign at school, on top of my normal teaching load. Since then it’s just… been there.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing or find pleasurable over the past year and a half?

Yeah… I have. I used to actually look forward to things like softball, book club, my garden… even helping with robotics club.

Now I either cancel, or I show up and just sort of… get through it. It doesn’t really feel enjoyable anymore.
Do you still find any activities pleasurable or is everything feeling unenjoyable lately?

Honestly… not really. I mean, maybe little moments here and there, but the things I used to look forward to—softball, book club, my garden, robotics club—I mostly just cancel or show up and go through the motions. It doesn’t feel enjoyable anymore.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year and a half?
Yeah… a bit. I haven’t been weighing myself much, but my clothes are definitely looser. Most school days I just… don’t eat until late afternoon, not really on purpose.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you've been moving around over the past year and a half?

Yeah… my energy’s been pretty low. After teaching all day and then sitting through a department meeting, I just feel… heavy. Like even making dinner or replying to a few parent emails feels like a lot.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past year and a half?

Yeah… sleep hasn’t been great. I’ll be exhausted, but then I’m just lying there thinking about deadlines or things I said wrong in class. And I wake up really early, like around 4, and… usually don’t properly fall back asleep.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Yeah… I do. Probably more than I should.

If a lesson goes badly, or a student looks confused, I sort of… take it as proof that I’m not doing my job properly. Then I replay it later and it turns into, you know, I’m letting everyone down. At school and at home. Like I’m a terrible teacher and… mother.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything obvious like that… maybe I’m a bit slower when I’m tired, but I don’t know if it’s enough to count.
Have you been feeling irritable or short-tempered more often than usual over the past year and a half?
I don’t know… not especially. I mean, I get stressed, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed being more short-tempered than usual.
Have you had any trouble concentrating on things like lesson plans, reading, or other tasks that require focus over the past year and a half?

Yes… I think so. It’s been harder than it used to be.

Like, I’ll read the same student answer three or four times and still feel like I don’t know what mark to give it. And even simple things—like deciding which lab supplies to order—can take me ages. I just sort of get stuck.
Have you noticed yourself feeling restless or having an inability to sit still?
Not really… I don’t think so. I’m not pacing around or anything. I can sit still, as far as I’ve noticed.
Have you had thoughts of death itself, not just wondering if others would be better off without you, over the past year and a half?

Yes… I have. Not all the time, but I’ve caught myself thinking it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up.

And… sometimes driving home, I wonder if my family or my students would be better off without me. I don’t want to do anything, but it scares me that I’m even thinking that.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes… I have. I used to really look forward to softball and book club, and working in my garden.

Now I mostly just… show up because I’m supposed to, or I cancel. Even robotics club feels like I’m just going through the motions. It doesn’t really feel enjoyable anymore.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities?

Yes… for more than two weeks. I just haven’t really cared about things I used to enjoy—softball, book club, gardening. Even robotics club… I mostly just go through the motions now, or cancel. It doesn’t feel like much of anything.
Have you had a period of time in the past year and a half where your depressive symptoms were significantly worse for at least two weeks?

Yes. It’s… been going on about a year and seven months, I think. Since I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my normal teaching load. It got pretty bad for longer than two weeks during that time.
Do you feel like you've lost pleasure in almost all activities most of the time over the past year and a half?

Yeah… most of the time. Things like softball, book club, my garden… even robotics club. I used to look forward to them, and now I mostly just go because I should, or I cancel. It doesn’t really feel enjoyable anymore.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks in the recent past where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities?

Yes. I mean… I’ve kind of said it already, but I just don’t get much out of things anymore. Softball, book club, gardening, robotics club… I used to look forward to them, and now I either cancel or just show up and go through the motions.
Have you had any periods where your depressive symptoms significantly improved for at least two months since they started about a year and a half ago?
I don’t think so. Not for that long, anyway. There might’ve been a few easier days here and there, but I can’t really point to two months where it felt significantly better.
